motion_rule: the washing line itself runs through its pulley all clip and carries her down the yard while sheets, banknotes and the two crows tear across the lens every beat; the camera tracks alongside, her head half the frame; new shot size each beat, never wider than her head filling a third of frame, one action per beat, no bars
character: a slim grey turtle dove, pink breast, black neck ring, head stabbing the air
second_characters: two rangy crows in flat caps with knives, a wing from the lens, cutting across the line and dropping on the sack at 7.60
props: ONE fat sack of notes on a cord round her toe, dragging her along the line from the first beat; A SWARM of banknotes tearing out of it
prop_continuity: the sack rides on her toe to 6.45, swinging heavier every beat, and hits the grass at 7.05
environment: a yard at noon, washing lines strung wall to wall a wing away both sides, sheets packed along them, grass below, no empty distance
light_events: blazing white sun on the yard and the sheets to 1.75; at 1.75 the storm wall rams over and the yard drops to slate grey, her face and the sack still bright

audio.language: Russian, lines verbatim; latin hints never spoken
audio.delivery: a soft cooing female voice gone hard, preaching, biting each word, 4 syllables/sec
audio.pronunciation: ot-LO-zhish, na CHOR-ny den, pri-DYOT, CHOR-na-ya noch, DEN-gi, ne spa-SUT, TOL-ko, KRY-lya
audio.pacing: 0.00-1.75, 2.15-3.75 and 4.15-6.45 each one breath; after 6.45 not a word, sfx keep going
audio.lip_sync: her beak opens wide and shapes every syllable, throat swelling
audio.sfx: wind, sheets cracking, the line running through its pulley, thunder, knives scraping

timeline.a: the line jerks into motion through its pulley and carries her down the yard, sheets slapping past
the sack swings out wide and drags her along the running line, the hedge tearing past behind
the storm wall rams over the yard and the sun goes out of the grass in one sweep
she snaps her head round and the line bucks under her feet
she rides the other way as sheets rip off the line and blow across the frame
both crows drop onto the running line either side of her, knives up
she squares her shoulders and shoves the sack out along the line
a knife rakes the line beside her toe and banknotes tear out of the sack at the lens
she rises on her toes, wings half lifting, the cord going tight
she throws both wings wide and the line whips out from under her
she lets the cord go and climbs, the sack falling away below her
the sack slams into the grass and bursts, banknotes blowing up around it
both crows drop on the sack in the grass, knives out, tearing at it, while she climbs at the lens above them
she banks across the lens, wings filling the frame, the crows below rolling over the sack
the crows claw the empty sack apart, notes blowing past, she a shrinking shape over the storm

must_appear: the sack on her toe to 6.45; full sun on the yard to 1.75 and the storm wall over it from 2.15; at 7.05 the sack hits the grass; at 7.60 both crows drop on it with knives while her face and open wings fill the frame above
negative_prompt: subtitles, watermark, letterbox, cyrillic letters, words, a parked camera, a still washing line, a closed beak while speaking, slow motion, a camera pulling back, a bird hanging motionless, an unreadable dark frame, a foreign accent, a word not in the lines
